_note: Substances/routes where a data source's DOSE ladder is skipped at ingest, so the next-priority source backfills. A declarative override (with a reason) instead of duplicating corrected dose data in the curated layer. Omit `routes` to skip that source's doses for the whole substance. Full candidate list from the dc/PW/TripSit audit: /tmp/piru-dose-audit/dc-dose-issues.csv — these should also be reported upstream for a real fix.

drug.community.name: 2C-E
drug.community.note: dc row is an empty placeholder (no tiers).

drug.community.name: 2C-F
drug.community.note: dc ships threshold 100 / common 350-500 / heavy 750 mg. PIHKAL #26 gives "DOSAGE: greater than 250 mg" and "DURATION: unknown" — Shulgin tried graded doses and found no convincing central effects at any of them. There is no known active dose to ladder.

drug.community.name: Amobarbital
drug.community.note: dc IV common > oral — implausible for a barbiturate.

drug.community.name: Atropine
drug.community.note: common 2-5 / strong 6-10 mg. Anticholinergic therapeutic dosing tops out ~2 mg and 6-10 mg is potentially lethal (LDLo ~1-4 mg/kg). Only source for the oral route; the IV antidote ladder is correct and stays.

drug.community.name: Bromoketamine
drug.community.note: threshold 0.3 / common 0.7-1 mg against this same source's own insufflation ladder of 90-160 mg — a 100x internal contradiction, almost certainly mg/kg recorded as absolute mg. The substance is tagged no-human-data.

drug.community.name: Cocaine
drug.community.note: dc IV ~6x too high — copies the insufflation ladder; IV should be lower.

drug.community.name: Ketamine
drug.community.note: dc insufflation ladder incomplete and odd (T28, missing strong/heavy).

drug.community.name: MXP
drug.community.note: drug.community files this as "MXP (Methoxphenidine)", so the exception keys on the split short name. MXP is documented oral and insufflated only — not formulated or characterized for injection. Offering an IV ladder is an invitation, not a reference.

drug.community.name: Para-Methoxyamphetamine
drug.community.note: PMA under its full name. Documented adverse/lethal exposure overlaps the range this source calls "common", so there is no window left to ladder. Dropped rather than re-numbered — no source gives a defensible ladder and inventing one is the failure mode this file exists to stop.

drug.community.name: PCP
drug.community.note: total 4-8 h is the insufflated/smoked profile; oral PCP runs 6-24 h. Under-stating it is a re-dose risk on a drug with a long, unpleasant tail.

drug.community.name: Quetiapine
drug.community.note: dc common ~2.5–5x above the FDA-labeled range for this antipsychotic.

_erowid_note: The PIHKAL/TIHKAL importer turns a single stated figure into a `common` band of [0.75x, 1.25x]. Where Shulgin's DOSAGE field is a real range ("12 - 25 mg") the importer reproduces it exactly — 78 of 78 shipped rows verified against the book text. Where the field is a no-activity bound ("greater than 250 mg", "unknown") the same transform publishes the dose at which NOTHING happened as the typical dose: 2C-F showed "common 187.5-312.5 mg" for a compound Shulgin never found active, and DMT showed "common 262.5-437.5 mg" ORAL for a compound that is orally inactive without an MAOI. The entries below are every such row, generated by matching the shipped ladders against the book's own DOSAGE lines; the note carries that line verbatim.

psychonautwiki.name: Acetylfentanyl
psychonautwiki.note: common 10-15 mg on a fentanyl analog ~1/3 fentanyl's potency, whose active dose is therefore a few hundred MICROGRAMS. The shown common tier is 30-100x an active dose and far above documented fatal exposure — an mg/ug scale error upstream. Documented adverse/lethal exposure overlaps the range this source calls "common", so there is no window left to ladder. Dropped rather than re-numbered — no source gives a defensible ladder and inventing one is the failure mode this file exists to stop.

psychonautwiki.name: CDP-Choline
psychonautwiki.note: total 58-74 h, offset 30-40 h, afterglow 40-60 h for a nootropic whose effects run hours. piru-curated (8-24 h) already outranks the total, but per-phase resolution meant the bad offset and afterglow still resolved from here — masking is not fixing.

psychonautwiki.name: Citicoline
psychonautwiki.note: PsychonautWiki's own name for CDP-Choline. It ingests as its own row and is only merged into CDP-Choline afterwards, so at ingest time neither the record name nor the resolved canonical is "CDP-Choline" — the exception has to name it here. Same values as the CDP-Choline entry.

psychonautwiki.name: Midazolam
psychonautwiki.note: peak 1-4 h on the drug chosen for procedural sedation precisely because it peaks in minutes (t1/2 1.5-2.5 h). drug.community's 15 min backfills.

psychonautwiki.name: Naloxone
psychonautwiki.note: Oral bioavailability ~2%; naloxone is IN Suboxone precisely because it is systemically inactive by mouth. A 5-15 min onset and 1-2 h total for oral dosing is pharmacokinetically impossible, and offering the route at all implies an opioid reversal that will not happen.

psychonautwiki.name: Nifoxipam
psychonautwiki.note: total 10-75 h; the 75 h upper is implausible even for a nitro-benzodiazepine. TripSit's 10-18 h backfills.

psychonautwiki.name: PMA
psychonautwiki.note: threshold 10 / light 20-40 / common 40-60 mg and NO strong or heavy tier, which reads as "nothing above this is defined" rather than "above this kills". PMA/PMMA blood levels >0.5 mg/L are toxic-to-lethal against a fatal median of 1.92 mg/L. Documented adverse/lethal exposure overlaps the range this source calls "common", so there is no window left to ladder. Dropped rather than re-numbered — no source gives a defensible ladder and inventing one is the failure mode this file exists to stop.

psychonautwiki.name: PMMA
psychonautwiki.note: a single 100-120 mg "common" tier already inside the reported lethal range; recreational and lethal exposure overlap with no separable window. Documented adverse/lethal exposure overlaps the range this source calls "common", so there is no window left to ladder. Dropped rather than re-numbered — no source gives a defensible ladder and inventing one is the failure mode this file exists to stop.

tripsit.name: 4,4-DMAR
tripsit.note: common 60-120 mg. Glanville 2015 (Hum Psychopharmacol) records unwanted effects from 5 mg against desired effects at 10-200 mg — the ranges fully overlap — and 4,4-DMAR is linked to 31 European deaths in nine months. Documented adverse/lethal exposure overlaps the range this source calls "common", so there is no window left to ladder. Dropped rather than re-numbered — no source gives a defensible ladder and inventing one is the failure mode this file exists to stop.

tripsit.name: Acetylfentanyl
tripsit.note: common 3-5 mg — still ~10x an active dose for a fentanyl analog and inside documented fatal oral exposure. Documented adverse/lethal exposure overlaps the range this source calls "common", so there is no window left to ladder. Dropped rather than re-numbered — no source gives a defensible ladder and inventing one is the failure mode this file exists to stop.

tripsit.name: Allobarbital
tripsit.note: light 500-1000 / common 1000-1500 / strong 1500-2000 mg for an intermediate-acting barbiturate whose hypnotic dose was ~100-200 mg (Cibalgin tablets carried 40-60 mg). The whole ladder sits in the lethal zone and TripSit is the only source, so it goes rather than being re-numbered.

tripsit.name: Changa
tripsit.note: Changa is a DMT-infused smoking blend; an oral route is a categorical error. Its ladder (5-50 mg) and timeline (onset 0-2 min, total 6-12 min) are the SMOKED values mis-assigned. Oral DMT without an MAOI does nothing at all.

tripsit.name: Midazolam
tripsit.note: total 4-8 h is a long-acting benzo's profile; midazolam's t1/2 is 1.5-2.5 h and it is chosen clinically FOR its ultra-short action.

tripsit.name: Propoxyphene
tripsit.note: total 1-3 h against t1/2 6-12 h (norpropoxyphene ~30-36 h) — about a quarter of the true duration, on a drug withdrawn for cardiotoxicity.

tripsit.name: Sufentanil
tripsit.note: total 5-10 min is the IV profile inherited verbatim. Oral BA ~12%, absorbed over 30-90 min. A user reading "10 minutes" on an ultra-potent opioid could fatally re-dose.

tripsit.name: Triazolam
tripsit.note: strong ceiling 1.5 mg is 3x the FDA-labeled MAXIMUM of 0.5 mg/day (Halcion label 2.1). freeodwiki's 0.5-0.75 backfills and sits at the label ceiling.
